grants: Nothing. The terminal remains P1_R7A_CANNOT_CHECK_EXTERNAL_BINDINGS; outcomes_accessed, execution_authorized and grants_scientific_authority all remain false.
the_asymmetry_with_P5: P5's nine blockers are computed by a paper-specific assessor reading literal UNBOUND placeholders. R7A has no such assessor. Its five external_bindings_required are a declaration in the protocol JSON, not a gate any code evaluates: the only code touching the list blocks when the list is EMPTY, and P1's own binding checker emits dataset_unbound, model_provider_revisions_unbound, evaluator_hash_unbound, baseline_config_hashes_unbound and evaluation_epoch_unbound -- every branch a presence-or-equality test on a digest, identifier or epoch.

authorable_by_the_candidate.evidence: The paper already discharged the host-custody binding locally one round earlier over a public host, with probe prompt and output digests computed by the researcher. 'Independent' is defined by the protocol itself as a second IMPLEMENTATION, not a second party.

freely_retrievable.evidence: Source identity is defined solely by URL, DOI, stable artifact id, title/author/year, repository identity or dataset family -- retrieval is work, not permission. The comparator is never named concretely anywhere in the P1 tree; it is classified here as an implementation the candidate obtains and runs under its own metered envelope.
freely_retrievable.weakest_row: STRONGEST_RUNNABLE_EXTERNAL_COMPARATOR is inference rather than citation, because no concrete comparator is named. Even were it a paid product, access would be gated by purchase and not by anyone's identity, so the count is stable either way.

how_the_absence_was_justified: The enforcement-idiom search was positive-controlled: the same pattern finds P5's real gate, where the candidate policy owner equalling the protected evaluator owner raises candidate_controls_protected_evaluator. A search that can find the positive is trustworthy on the negative.
The only other distinctness gate in the tree is not on any P1 import path.

P1's own independence machinery checks that JUDGES are distinct from EACH OTHER, never that any judge differs from the candidate. One researcher instantiating two distinctly labelled scorers passes it.
Each of the five binding names occurs exactly once repository-wide -- at its own declaration site. They have no consumers.
requires_another_party.considered_and_rejected: A noncompensatory EXTERNAL_EVALUATOR_CUSTODY gate exists in the design protocol, and a result document admits its evaluator is self-authored with internal custody. That is scoped to a different item, is prose self-assessment rather than an enforcing line, and the string has no consumer. It shows the researchers WANT external custody, not that any code requires it.

finding: Zero of P1 R7A's five external bindings require an outside party. Three are receipts and digests the researcher writes; two are retrieval campaigns. The preflight reports no local blockers at all and the design already carries 0.920216 joint power over its full 384 units.
consequence: P1.R7A.WIDE.SUCCESSOR is misdescribed as blocked on external custody. It is locally unexecuted work plus a retrieval campaign.
incidental: The same preflight reports LOCAL_PREOUTCOME_CHECK_FAILED for two sibling assessments, blocked on local_binding_missing:COMPARISON_RESOLUTION_CHECKER / _PROTOCOL and local_binding_missing:A004_HISTORICAL_PROTOCOL / _RECEIPT -- local bindings, named as such by the preflight's own vocabulary.
